clue.text: Mistletoe, say, in place where soldier lands?

parts.note: a para is a paratrooper, a soldier who lands by parachute
a site is a place or location

explanation.surface: A botanist wonders whether mistletoe grows where paratroopers come down.
explanation.walkthrough: The wordplay reads 'place where soldier lands' as the para's site, the ground a paratrooper drops on to; 'where' and 'lands' only colour that picture.
explanation.definitionFit: Mistletoe lives on a host tree and draws nourishment from it, the textbook botanical example of such an organism.

clue.text: Fairly good-looking

explanation.surface: Someone is described as reasonably attractive.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adverb it means quite or rather; as an adjective, attractive.

clue.text: Sport in county division

explanation.walkthrough: Yorkshire, an English county, was split into North, East and West divisions with this name.
explanation.definitionFit: Horse-riding is a sport; Yorkshire was historically divided into three administrative areas with this name.

clue.text: Frighten sick at first with worry

indicators.note: at first means only the opening letter of the word sick is used

parts.note: care is worry or anxiety

explanation.surface: An illness alarms someone, at first making them anxious.
explanation.definitionFit: To alarm or startle someone, making them afraid.

clue.text: Worst place for F1 driver to enter?

explanation.surface: A racing driver dreads pulling in for a pit stop.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom for the very worst; also the pit lane where Formula One drivers stop for tyres and fuel.

clue.text: Part of plant shows bad sign

explanation.surface: A gardener notes that a part of the plant is showing a worrying symptom.
explanation.definitionFit: In botany it is the part of the pistil that receives pollen; generally it is a mark of disgrace or shame.

clue.text: What may come off the back of a lorry

definitions.text: What may come off the back of a lorry

parts.words: What may come off the back of a lorry
parts.note: the British phrase suggests stolen goods, but here it is the hinged flap at a truck's rear

explanation.walkthrough: 'Fell off the back of a lorry' is British slang for goods of dubious, probably stolen, origin; a lorry is a truck.
explanation.definitionFit: A hinged board at the rear of a truck that can be let down or removed for loading.

clue.text: Confessed Matt died in agony

indicators.note: being in agony means writhing, so the letters of the two names are twisted

explanation.surface: Matt admitted his guilt before dying in pain.
explanation.definitionFit: To have owned up to something is to have acknowledged it.

clue.text: Glued to book, one looks blank

definitions.text: Glued to book, one looks blank

parts.words: Glued to book, one looks blank
parts.note: describes the plain sheet pasted inside a book's cover, which carries no printing

explanation.definitionFit: Bookbinders paste a blank leaf to the inside of each cover, joining the text block to the binding.

clue.text: Win over, when I'd turn jolly

indicators.note: the two words 'when' and 'I'd' are turned round together, read from the right

parts.note: as can mean when, as in 'as I left'
I'd is written ID without the apostrophe
a Jolly is old slang for a Royal Marine, abbreviated RM

explanation.surface: Someone hopes to charm a crowd by becoming cheerful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turn' reverses AS + ID to give DISA; 'jolly' is not cheerful but the slang for a Royal Marine (RM).
explanation.definitionFit: To win someone over is to remove their hostility, to take away their defences.

clue.text: Throw son into fountain for joke

indicators.note: son is thrown into the fountain, put inside the word for it

parts.note: a jet is a spout of water, as from a fountain

explanation.surface: Throwing a boy into the fountain was meant as a prank.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Throw' and 'into' together put S inside JET.
explanation.definitionFit: A jest is a joke or a witty remark.

clue.text: Characteristic smell, before drinking in fruit

parts.note: a tang is a sharp distinctive smell or taste

indicators.note: something drinking another takes it inside, so one word is placed within the other

parts.note: ere is a poetic word for before
taken as written

explanation.surface: A distinctive aroma comes before one tastes the fruit drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drinking' puts IN inside ERE to give ERINE, which follows TANG.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a small, loose-skinned orange-coloured citrus fruit, a kind of mandarin.

clue.text: Wait a little time for fixture

parts.note: to bide is to wait, as in 'bide your time'
T is the standard abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A fan waits a moment before a sports fixture begins.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fixture' suggests a sporting match, but it means a fitted item of bathroom plumbing.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a low basin plumbed into a bathroom, a permanent fitting.

clue.text: Look at ship's destruction

parts.note: lo is an old word meaning look or behold
SS stands for steamship, a prefix on ship names

explanation.surface: Onlookers watch a vessel being wrecked.
explanation.definitionFit: Destruction of something means it is gone, a deprivation or ruin.

clue.text: As member of team, keeping article so dishonestly acquired

indicators.note: keeping means holding, so one piece is held inside the other

parts.note: onside means on the same team, in agreement
the is the definite article

explanation.surface: A team member hangs on to illicitly obtained goods.
explanation.definitionFit: Something got illicitly, as extra earnings or an affair, is obtained secretly beyond what is legitimate.

clue.text: During suspension of hostilities, notice slander

indicators.note: one thing during another sits within it, so a short word goes inside a longer one

parts.note: a truce is a pause in fighting
an ad is a notice or advertisement

explanation.surface: In a ceasefire, a public notice spreads lies about the enemy.
explanation.definitionFit: To traduce someone is to speak ill of them falsely, to defame them.

clue.text: Mugs find a way into army vehicles

indicators.note: a way goes into the army vehicles, placed inside that word

parts.note: tanks are armoured army vehicles
RD is the abbreviation for road, a way

explanation.surface: Soldiers find a route through a column of armoured vehicles.
explanation.definitionFit: Large drinking vessels for beer, often with a handle.

clue.text: Say more about bad poet being approved

indicators.note: the phrase for saying more goes around the rearranged word

parts.note: to add is to say more, as in 'he added that...'

indicators.note: bad here signals the poet's letters are spoiled into a new order

explanation.surface: A critic keeps on talking about a terrible poet who nonetheless gets accepted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bad' rearranges POET as OPTE, and 'about' puts that inside ADD.
explanation.definitionFit: Something formally accepted or taken up, as a motion is, has been endorsed.

clue.text: Composer's last piece

parts.note: not a composer's final work, but the closing passage a composer writes at the end of a movement

explanation.definitionFit: In music it is the concluding section that rounds off a piece.

clue.text: Hypocrisy over a brief thanksgiving for work for the church

indicators.note: in a down clue one piece sitting over another comes before it

parts.note: cant is hypocritical, sanctimonious talk
ta is a short British word for thank you

explanation.surface: Sanctimony overshadows a short thanksgiving service in church.
explanation.definitionFit: A choral composition, often sacred, as Bach wrote for church services.

clue.text: Make every effort with tune

explanation.surface: A singer works hard at a melody.
explanation.definitionFit: To exert oneself to the utmost; also a passage of melody or music.

clue.text: Buy shares in clothing

parts.note: taken as written
a vest is an item of clothing

explanation.surface: Someone puts money into a fashion company.
explanation.walkthrough: 'clothing' looks like the business sector, but supplies VEST.
explanation.definitionFit: To put money into stocks or shares expecting profit.

clue.text: Scoundrel that can beat ten?

explanation.definitionFit: A rogue or rascal; also the jack in playing cards, which ranks above the ten.

clue.text: A number of French in pontoon

explanation.walkthrough: Pontoon is the British name for the card game also called blackjack.
explanation.definitionFit: The French for twenty-one, and the card game where players aim for a total of twenty-one, called pontoon in Britain.

clue.text: Back in a while — about one -to sell to public

indicators.note: the turned phrase goes about the digit, holding it inside
back signals the phrase for later is written backwards

parts.note: in a while means later
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A shopkeeper posts a 'back soon' sign before going to sell goods.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Back' reverses LATER to give RETAL, and 'about' places I inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: To sell in small quantities directly to consumers, as shops do.

clue.text: Nobleman's ruin -serious

parts.note: to mar is to spoil or ruin
grave means serious or solemn

explanation.surface: An aristocrat's downfall is a grave matter.
explanation.definitionFit: It was a German title of nobility, a count ruling a border province.

clue.text: Straw in mug

explanation.surface: Someone finds a drinking straw left in a cup.
explanation.definitionFit: A drinking tube through which one sucks; and a gullible person easily fooled.

clue.text: Upset neat, trim disciplinarian

indicators.note: upset means knocked over, so the letters of the two words are overturned into a new order

explanation.surface: A strict officer is annoyed by a tidy haircut.
explanation.definitionFit: A strict enforcer of rules, named after a French drillmaster.
